components.note: 幸 (luck) — often read as an old picture of shackles; 'luck' is escaping punishment. The dictionary story (one alive 土, one dead 干) is a memory aid.
土 (earth) — the top. Memory aid: the one standing on solid ground 土 is the lucky one — 幸运, 幸福.
子 (child) — children and offspring: 孩 child, 学 study, 孙 grandchild; 存 means to keep or survive.
才 (cái) is only a loose sound hint for cún.

example.hanzi: 那场事故中只有三个人幸存。
example.pinyin: nà chǎng shìgù zhōng zhǐyǒu sān gè rén xìngcún.
example.english: Only three people survived that accident.
example.fact: Of the roughly 2,224 passengers and crew aboard the Titanic when it sank in 1912, only about 706 survived, largely because the ship carried lifeboat capacity for barely half of everyone on board. The disaster led directly to international maritime law requiring ships to carry enough lifeboats for every person aboard, a rule still in force today.

examples.hanzi: 他是那次沉船事故的唯一幸存者。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì nà cì chénchuán shìgù de wéiyī xìngcún zhě.
examples.english: He was the only survivor of that shipwreck.

examples.hanzi: 这座古建筑奇迹般地幸存了下来。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò gǔ jiànzhù qíjì bān de xìngcún le xiàlái.
examples.english: This old building survived miraculously.

components.note: 十 (ten) — a cross: first a single vertical line, later crossed with a horizontal bar. Seen in 十分, 二十, and in 千.
二 (two) — the top and bottom bars. Dictionary story: five elements between heaven and earth, with a cross in the middle; memory aid, not firmly attested.

example.hanzi: 教室里一共坐了十五个学生。
example.pinyin: jiàoshì lǐ yígòng zuò le shíwǔ gè xuésheng.
example.english: There are fifteen students sitting in the classroom in total.
example.fact: The Moon takes about 29.5 days to cycle through its phases from new moon to new moon, so the full moon reliably falls near the midpoint of that cycle, around day fourteen or fifteen. That timing depends on the Moon being on the exact opposite side of Earth from the Sun, fully lit as seen from the ground.

examples.hanzi: 每个月的十五号是我们开会的日子。
examples.pinyin: Měi gè yuè de shíwǔ hào shì wǒmen kāihuì de rìzi.
examples.english: The fifteenth of each month is our meeting day.

examples.hanzi: 他今年十五岁，已经很高了。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīnnián shíwǔ suì, yǐjīng hěn gāo le.
examples.english: He is fifteen this year and already very tall.

components.note: 犭 (beast, form of 犬 dog) — animals: 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狼 wolf; 犯 is to attack or violate, hence offend.
见 (see) — 见 as in 现, 观, 觉; 规 first meant a compass, the drawing tool that sets the standard — hence rules, as in 规矩 compass and square.
夫 (fū) — loose sound hint — 规 is guī.

example.hanzi: 那名球员因犯规被罚下场。
example.pinyin: nà míng qiúyuán yīn fànguī bèi fá xiàchǎng.
example.english: That player was sent off for committing a foul.
example.fact: The NBA introduced the 24-second shot clock in 1954 after a nearly unwatchable 1950 game ended 19-18, with the leading team simply holding the ball and forcing fouls to run out the clock. The shot clock forced teams to attempt a shot within the time limit, transforming the pace and strategy of professional basketball almost overnight.

examples.hanzi: 裁判吹哨说他犯规了。
examples.pinyin: Cáipàn chuīshào shuō tā fànguī le.
examples.english: The referee blew his whistle and said he had committed a foul.

examples.hanzi: 开车闯红灯是犯规的行为。
examples.pinyin: Kāichē chuǎng hóngdēng shì fànguī de xíngwéi.
examples.english: Running a red light while driving is breaking the rules.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — cloth and clothing, as in 布 cloth, 带 belt, 帽 hat; 常 first meant a long skirt (裳 cháng).
尚 (shàng) is a loose sound clue for cháng; 尚 also sounds out 堂 táng and 掌 zhǎng.
见 (see) — 见 as in 现, 观, 觉; 规 first meant a compass, the drawing tool that sets the standard — hence rules, as in 规矩 compass and square.
夫 (fū) — loose sound hint — 规 is guī.

example.hanzi: 医生建议她做一次常规体检。
example.pinyin: yīshēng jiànyì tā zuò yí cì chángguī tǐjiǎn.
example.english: The doctor recommended she have a routine physical checkup.
example.fact: The commonly cited "normal" human body temperature of 37°C (98.6°F) comes from an 1868 study by German physician Carl Wunderlich, who compiled over a million temperature readings from thousands of patients. Modern research suggests average body temperature has actually drifted slightly lower since then, though 37°C remains the standard reference point in routine medical care.

examples.hanzi: 这是一个常规的检查，不用担心。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yī gè chángguī de jiǎnchá, bù yòng dānxīn.
examples.english: This is a routine checkup, so don't worry.

examples.hanzi: 他的做法打破了常规。
examples.pinyin: Tā de zuòfǎ dǎpò le chángguī.
examples.english: His approach broke with convention.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — hand holding a stick, as in 教 teach, 收 collect, 放 release: correcting by hand.
己 (jǐ) is a close sound clue for gǎi.
羊 (sheep) — 羊 is a symbol of good fortune, as in 美 and 祥; 善 is goodness and kindness, together with 口 (words).

example.hanzi: 新政策大大改善了居民的生活条件。
example.pinyin: xīn zhèngcè dàdà gǎishàn le jūmín de shēnghuó tiáojiàn.
example.english: The new policy greatly improved residents' living conditions.
example.fact: Toyota's production philosophy of "kaizen," or continuous incremental improvement, encourages every worker on the assembly line — not just managers — to stop production and suggest fixes the moment they spot a problem. The approach, developed in Japan after World War II, became a foundation of modern lean manufacturing practiced by companies worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 我们需要改善办公室的环境。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào gǎishàn bàngōngshì de huánjìng.
examples.english: We need to improve the office environment.

examples.hanzi: 多吃蔬菜可以改善你的健康状况。
examples.pinyin: Duō chī shūcài kěyǐ gǎishàn nǐ de jiànkāng zhuàngkuàng.
examples.english: Eating more vegetables can improve your health.

components.note: 酉 (wine jar) — fermented drinks and flavors: 醉 drunk, 醒 sober, 酸 sour, 配 match; 酒 is liquor, with 氵 for the liquid.
酉 also hints at the sound: yǒu is close to jiǔ.
后 (after, behind) — two words merged in simplified writing: old 后 "ruler" (皇后 empress) and 後 "behind, later" (as in 然后).

example.hanzi: 酒后驾车是非常危险的行为。
example.pinyin: jiǔhòu jiàchē shì fēicháng wēixiǎn de xíngwéi.
example.english: Driving after drinking is an extremely dangerous behavior.
example.fact: The first practical breathalyzer, developed by American police captain and biochemist Robert Borkenstein in 1954, measured blood alcohol content by having a driver breathe into a balloon connected to a chemical solution that changed color in proportion to alcohol concentration. His device gave law enforcement a fast, roadside way to estimate impairment for the first time, replacing earlier tests that required a hospital blood draw.

examples.hanzi: 酒后不要开车，要叫代驾。
examples.pinyin: Jiǔ hòu bù yào kāichē, yào jiào dàijià.
examples.english: Don't drive after drinking, call a designated driver.

examples.hanzi: 他酒后说了很多心里话。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiǔ hòu shuō le hěn duō xīnlǐhuà.
examples.english: After drinking, he said many things from the heart.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
口 (mouth) — eating and speech: 喝, 吸, 吗; 吃 is to eat.
乞 (qǐ) is only a loose sound clue for chī.
一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 怕, 情, 快; 惊 is a startled heart.
京 (jīng) sounds exactly like 惊; also in 鲸 jīng and 景 jǐng.

example.hanzi: 听到那个消息,他大吃一惊。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào nàge xiāoxi, tā dà chī yī jīng.
example.english: Hearing that news, he was astounded.
example.fact: The 1883 eruption of Krakatoa produced a sound so loud it ruptured eardrums 40 miles away and was heard as far as 3,000 miles away in Australia — one of the loudest sounds ever recorded in human history. Sailors caught in the shockwave were astounded to see the sky turn pitch black at midday, and the blast triggered tsunamis that killed tens of thousands of people along the surrounding coasts.

examples.hanzi: 看到成绩单，妈妈大吃一惊。
examples.pinyin: Kàndào chéngjìdān, māma dà chī yī jīng.
examples.english: Mom was taken aback when she saw the report card.

examples.hanzi: 他突然出现在门口，我们都大吃一惊。
examples.pinyin: Tā tūrán chūxiàn zài ménkǒu, wǒmen dōu dà chī yī jīng.
examples.english: He suddenly showed up at the door, and we were all astounded.

components.note: 长 (long, grow) — simplified from 長, an old person with long hair. Read cháng "long" or zhǎng "to grow, elder".
目 (eye) — looking; an eye turned on a tree 木, hence to look at, and mutually looking: "each other". 相 also gives 想 xiǎng, 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.

example.hanzi: 他的长相很像他父亲。
example.pinyin: Tā de zhǎngxiàng hěn xiàng tā fùqīn.
example.english: His appearance closely resembles his father's.
example.fact: Studies of identical twins raised apart show that facial appearance is among the most heritable human traits, with genetics accounting for the large majority of variation in features like nose shape and jawline. Researchers have even found that subtle habits tied to appearance, such as a particular smile or squint, can run in families across generations.

examples.hanzi: 她的长相很甜，笑起来有两个酒窝。
examples.pinyin: Tā de zhǎngxiàng hěn tián, xiào qǐlái yǒu liǎng gè jiǔwō.
examples.english: She has a sweet look, with two dimples when she smiles.

examples.hanzi: 你不能只看长相就判断一个人。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bù néng zhǐ kàn zhǎngxiàng jiù pànduàn yí gè rén.
examples.english: You can't judge a person just by their looks.

components.note: ⻊ (foot, form of 足) — feet and travel: 跑, 跳, 跟; 路 is a road.
各 (gè) is a loose sound clue; same part in 洛 luò, 落 luò, 客 kè.
易 (yì) is a loose sound clue for 踢 tī, 赐 cì and 惕 tì; the meaning "easy" comes from "change" and its early lizard picture is unproven.

example.hanzi: 路易十四统治法国长达七十二年。
example.pinyin: Lùyì Shísì tǒngzhì Fàguó chángdá qīshí'èr nián.
example.english: Louis XIV ruled France for seventy-two years.
example.fact: Louis XIV of France reigned for 72 years and 110 days, the longest confirmed reign of any monarch in European history. He transformed a modest hunting lodge at Versailles into a palace of over 2,300 rooms, and the rigid daily rituals of his court set the standard for European royal etiquette for generations afterward.

examples.hanzi: 路易是一位法国画家，住在巴黎。
examples.pinyin: Lùyì shì yí wèi Fǎguó huàjiā, zhù zài Bālí.
examples.english: Louis is a French painter who lives in Paris.

examples.hanzi: 我的邻居叫路易，他很喜欢养狗。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de línjū jiào Lùyì, tā hěn xǐhuan yǎng gǒu.
examples.english: My neighbor is called Louis, and he loves keeping dogs.

components.note: 北 — two people (匕) back to back; the meaning "north" is a later loan, and "back" survives in the reading bèi (败北 defeat).
阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 那: a district or ministry.
咅 (pǒu) is a loose sound clue for bù; 咅 also in 剖 pōu, 培 péi and 陪 péi.

example.hanzi: 挪威北部经常能看到北极光。
example.pinyin: Nuówēi běibù jīngcháng néng kàndào běijíguāng.
example.english: The northern part of Norway often has views of the aurora borealis.
example.fact: The aurora borealis occurs when charged particles from the sun collide with gases roughly 100 to 300 kilometers up in Earth's atmosphere, exciting oxygen and nitrogen atoms until they release light. Oxygen typically produces the green and red hues, while nitrogen creates blue and purple, which is why the sky over far-northern towns can shift color within seconds.

examples.hanzi: 这个国家的北部冬天特别冷。
examples.pinyin: Zhège guójiā de běibù dōngtiān tèbié lěng.
examples.english: The northern part of this country is especially cold in winter.

examples.hanzi: 我们打算去中国北部旅行。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen dǎsuàn qù Zhōngguó běibù lǚxíng.
examples.english: We plan to travel to northern China.

components.note: 米 (rice) — refined grain gives the idea of essence and the best part, hence 精 fine, spirit (精神).
青 (qīng) is a near sound match (-ing); the series 青 清 请 情 晴 静 helps recall jīng.
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.hanzi: 这座花园是园丁精心设计的。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò huāyuán shì yuándīng jīngxīn shèjì de.
example.english: This garden was meticulously designed by the gardener.
example.fact: The rock garden at Ryōan-ji temple in Kyoto contains only fifteen stones arranged across a bed of raked white gravel, yet from any spot on the viewing veranda at least one stone is always hidden from sight. Historians still debate whether this was a deliberate design choice or simply a side effect of the garden's centuries of meticulous upkeep.

examples.hanzi: 老师精心准备了今天的课。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī jīngxīn zhǔnbèi le jīntiān de kè.
examples.english: The teacher prepared today's lesson with great care.

examples.hanzi: 这是她精心挑选的生日礼物。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì tā jīngxīn tiāoxuǎn de shēngrì lǐwù.
examples.english: This is a birthday gift she carefully selected.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and worship: 神 god, 祝 wish, 福 fortune; 礼 are ritual courtesies.

example.hanzi: 他对服务员说话很无礼。
example.pinyin: Tā duì fúwùyuán shuōhuà hěn wúlǐ.
example.english: He spoke very rudely to the waiter.
example.fact: Victorian etiquette manuals of the 1830s devoted entire chapters to the precise angle of a bow and the correct way to greet a stranger, treating even minor breaches as evidence of poor character. Many of these codes were designed less to promote genuine courtesy than to mark class boundaries, since only the wealthy had the leisure to memorize hundreds of such rules.

examples.hanzi: 对长辈这样说话太无礼了。
examples.pinyin: Duì zhǎngbèi zhèyàng shuōhuà tài wúlǐ le.
examples.english: Talking to your elders like that is too rude.

examples.hanzi: 请原谅我刚才的无礼。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng yuánliàng wǒ gāngcái de wúlǐ.
examples.english: Please forgive my rudeness just now.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.
钅 (metal, simplified 金) — metals, as in 钱 money, 铁 iron, 铜 copper; 错 first meant to inlay metal.
昔 (xī) is a loose sound clue for cuò; 昔 also sounds out 借 jiè, 措 cuò and 惜 xī.

example.hanzi: 这次事故不是他的过错。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì shìgù bú shì tā de guòcuò.
example.english: This accident was not his fault.
example.fact: Alexander Fleming's discovery of penicillin in 1928 began with what he later called a careless mistake: he left a petri dish of bacteria uncovered while on vacation, and it became contaminated with mold. Rather than discard the ruined dish, he noticed the mold was killing the surrounding bacteria, a mishap that led directly to the first modern antibiotic.

examples.hanzi: 这次比赛输了，是我的过错。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì bǐsài shū le, shì wǒ de guòcuò.
examples.english: We lost this match, and it was my fault.

examples.hanzi: 他勇敢地承认了自己的过错。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒnggǎn de chéngrèn le zìjǐ de guòcuò.
examples.english: He bravely admitted his mistake.

components.note: 舟 (boat) — 舟 is a boat, as in 船, 般; 航 is sailing.
亢 (kàng) — near sound — 航 is háng; 亢 also sounds out 抗 kàng and 坑 kēng.

example.hanzi: 这趟航班晚点了。
example.pinyin: Zhè tàng hángbān wǎndiǎn le.
example.english: This flight is delayed.
example.fact: 航 originally meant a boat; now it covers flights and ships: 航班 (flight), 航空 (aviation), 航海 (sailing), 导航 (navigation) and 航天 (spaceflight).

examples.hanzi: 你坐哪个航班回去？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuò nǎge hángbān huíqù?
examples.english: Which flight are you taking back?

examples.hanzi: 轮船正在海上航行。
examples.pinyin: Lúnchuán zhèngzài hǎishàng hángxíng.
examples.english: The ship is sailing at sea.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 恶 is a bad heart, evil.
亚 (yà) is only a loose sound hint for è.
木 (wood) — a wooden stick; also in 树 tree, 林 forest.
昆 (kūn) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 混 hùn.

example.hanzi: 电影里的那个恶棍最后被警察抓住了。
example.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de nàge ègùn zuìhòu bèi jǐngchá zhuāzhù le.
example.english: The scoundrel in the movie was eventually caught by the police.
example.fact: Blackbeard, the English pirate Edward Teach, terrorized the Caribbean and American coast for only about two years before his death in 1718, yet he built his fearsome reputation largely through theatrics. He reportedly wove lit fuses into his beard during battle so that smoke curled around his face and made him look demonic to his victims.

examples.hanzi: 故事里的恶棍偷走了村民的粮食。
examples.pinyin: Gùshi lǐ de ègùn tōuzǒu le cūnmín de liángshi.
examples.english: The villain in the story stole the villagers' grain.

examples.hanzi: 别信他，他就是个恶棍。
examples.pinyin: Bié xìn tā, tā jiù shì gè ègùn.
examples.english: Don't trust him, he's a scoundrel.

components.note: 阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 部 part. 那 was a place name before it meant "that".
年 (year) — first drawn as a person carrying harvested grain: one harvest per year. Seen in 今年, 去年, 年轻.

example.hanzi: 那年夏天特别热。
example.pinyin: Nà nián xiàtiān tèbié rè.
example.english: That summer was especially hot.
example.fact: 2023 was confirmed as the hottest year on record globally, with average surface temperatures about 1.45°C above pre-industrial levels. Scientists linked much of the extreme heat to a strong El Niño event, a periodic shift that moves vast amounts of stored heat from the Pacific Ocean into the atmosphere.

examples.hanzi: 那年我刚上大学，一个人来到北京。
examples.pinyin: Nà nián wǒ gāng shàng dàxué, yí gè rén láidào Běijīng.
examples.english: That year I had just started university and came to Beijing alone.

examples.hanzi: 我还记得那年冬天下了很大的雪。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hái jìde nà nián dōngtiān xià le hěn dà de xuě.
examples.english: I still remember that winter it snowed heavily.

components.note: 牛 (ox) — leading an ox by a rope; as a part, 牛 marks cattle and animals, as in 物 thing, 特 special, 牧 herd.
氵 (water) — a stream to cross; also in 河 river, 游 swim.
步 (step) — steps through water: wading, hence being involved in something.

example.hanzi: 这个案子牵涉到好几个国家。
example.pinyin: Zhège ànzi qiānshè dào hǎo jǐ gè guójiā.
example.english: This case involves several countries.
example.fact: The 2016 Panama Papers leak involved more than 11.5 million documents from a single Panamanian law firm and implicated politicians, business leaders, and celebrities from over 200 countries and territories. It remains one of the largest data leaks in journalism history, compiled by more than 100 media organizations working together for over a year before publication.

examples.hanzi: 这件事牵涉到很多人的利益。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì qiānshè dào hěn duō rén de lìyì.
examples.english: This matter involves the interests of many people.

examples.hanzi: 我不想牵涉进他们的争吵。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎng qiānshè jìn tāmen de zhēngchǎo.
examples.english: I don't want to get dragged into their argument.

components.note: 阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 部 part. 那 was a place name before it meant "that".
殳 (strike) — 殳 is a hand with a tool striking, as in 毁, 殴; 段 is a piece cut off a larger whole, and sounds out 锻 duàn.

example.hanzi: 那段时间他每天都在图书馆学习。
example.pinyin: Nà duàn shíjiān tā měitiān dōu zài túshūguǎn xuéxí.
example.english: During that period, he studied at the library every day.
example.fact: When Cambridge University closed because of the plague in 1665 and 1666, Isaac Newton spent nearly two years working alone at his family's farm in Woolsthorpe. During that stretch, later called his 'annus mirabilis,' he laid the groundwork for calculus, the theory of gravity, and his early work on optics.

examples.hanzi: 那段路很难走，我们走了三个小时。
examples.pinyin: Nà duàn lù hěn nán zǒu, wǒmen zǒu le sān gè xiǎoshí.
examples.english: That stretch of road was hard to walk, and it took us three hours.

examples.hanzi: 那段时间我很忙，几乎没有休息。
examples.pinyin: Nà duàn shíjiān wǒ hěn máng, jīhū méiyǒu xiūxi.
examples.english: I was very busy during that period and hardly rested.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and liquids: 河, 海, 汤; 激 is water surging up, then to stir up.
敫 (jiǎo) is only a loose sound clue for jī.
心 (heart) — 心 marks emotions and thought, as in 想, 思, 急; 怒 is rage.
奴 (nú) — same sound, different tone — 怒 is nù; 奴 also sounds out 努 nǔ.

example.hanzi: 他的话激怒了在场的所有人。
example.pinyin: Tā de huà jīnù le zàichǎng de suǒyǒu rén.
example.english: His words infuriated everyone present.
example.fact: In December 1773, a new British tax on tea infuriated colonists in Boston so much that a group calling themselves the Sons of Liberty boarded three ships and dumped 342 chests of tea into the harbor. The tea, worth roughly $1.7 million in today's money, took weeks to wash ashore up and down the New England coast.

examples.hanzi: 别说那些话来激怒他。
examples.pinyin: Bié shuō nàxiē huà lái jīnù tā.
examples.english: Don't say those things to provoke him.

examples.hanzi: 老板的态度激怒了客人。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn de tàidù jīnù le kèrén.
examples.english: The boss's attitude angered the customers.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室.
女 (woman) — a woman at home under the roof: calm and safe.
东 (east) — simplified from 東; a common memory aid is the sun 日 caught in a tree 木 at sunrise.
尼 (ní) — 尼 sounds out 泥 ní and 呢 ní; here it appears mostly in foreign names such as 丹尼.

example.hanzi: 安东尼是我们班新来的交换生。
example.pinyin: Āndōngní shì wǒmen bān xīn lái de jiāohuànshēng.
example.english: Anthony is the new exchange student in our class.
example.fact: The Roman general Mark Antony formed a political and romantic alliance with Cleopatra of Egypt that ultimately clashed with Octavian's forces at the Battle of Actium in 31 BC. His defeat there marked the end of the Roman Republic's civil wars and the beginning of the Roman Empire under Augustus.

examples.hanzi: 安东尼喜欢踢足球，每个周末都去球场。
examples.pinyin: Āndōngní xǐhuan tī zúqiú, měi gè zhōumò dōu qù qiúchǎng.
examples.english: Anthony likes playing soccer and goes to the field every weekend.

examples.hanzi: 我给安东尼打了个电话。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi Āndōngní dǎ le gè diànhuà.
examples.english: I gave Anthony a phone call.

components.note: 大 (big) — an extra stroke below emphasises it: bigger than big, too much. 太 also sounds out 泰 tài.
平 (píng, flat) also lends its sound to 评 píng, 苹 píng and 坪 píng.
氵 (water) — 洋 is the ocean, as in 海 sea, 河 river.
羊 (yáng) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 样 yàng, 养 yǎng and 详 xiáng.

example.hanzi: 太平洋是世界上最大的海洋。
example.pinyin: Tàipíng Yáng shì shìjiè shàng zuì dà de hǎiyáng.
example.english: The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean in the world.
example.fact: The Pacific Ocean covers about 165 million square kilometers, more than all of Earth's land area combined. Its deepest point, the Mariana Trench's Challenger Deep, plunges nearly 11,000 meters below the surface — deep enough to submerge Mount Everest with room to spare.

examples.hanzi: 飞机飞越太平洋要十几个小时。
examples.pinyin: Fēijī fēiyuè Tàipíngyáng yào shí jǐ gè xiǎoshí.
examples.english: Flying across the Pacific takes more than ten hours.

examples.hanzi: 海豚生活在太平洋里。
examples.pinyin: Hǎitún shēnghuó zài Tàipíngyáng lǐ.
examples.english: Dolphins live in the Pacific Ocean.

components.note: 高 (tall) — a drawing of a tall tower building. 高 also sounds out 糕 gāo (cake), 搞 gǎo and 稿 gǎo.
尸 (a house shape) — roofs and buildings, as in 屋 room, 层 floor; the traditional 層 had 曾 céng for the sound, dropped in simplification.

example.hanzi: 这座城市有很多高层建筑。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì yǒu hěn duō gāocéng jiànzhù.
example.english: This city has many high-rise buildings.
example.fact: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai stands 828 meters tall, making it the world's tallest building since it opened in 2010. Its design was inspired by the geometric patterns of a desert flower called the Hymenocallis, and the building's spire alone is taller than the Eiffel Tower.

examples.hanzi: 他住在这栋楼的高层，风景很好。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhù zài zhè dòng lóu de gāocéng, fēngjǐng hěn hǎo.
examples.english: He lives on a high floor of this building, with a great view.

examples.hanzi: 公司高层今天开了一个会。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī gāocéng jīntiān kāi le yí gè huì.
examples.english: Senior management held a meeting today.

meanings: younger male cousin through a female relative

components.note: 衣 (clothes; 衤 on the left) — the outer garment.
毛 (fur) — a fur coat worn outside: the outside, the surface, then to show.
弟 (dì) is a sound clue for 第 dì, 梯 tī and 剃 tì; as a word it means younger brother.

example.hanzi: 我表弟比我小三岁。
example.pinyin: Wǒ biǎodì bǐ wǒ xiǎo sān suì.
example.english: My cousin is three years younger than me.
example.fact: Queen Victoria and Prince Albert, who married in 1840, were first cousins — a common practice among European royalty at the time meant to keep power within extended families. Geneticists later linked this same practice to the spread of hemophilia through several royal houses of Europe, traced back to Victoria herself.

examples.hanzi: 我表弟明年要考大学。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ biǎodì míngnián yào kǎo dàxué.
examples.english: My younger cousin will take the college entrance exam next year.

examples.hanzi: 表弟送了我一本很有意思的书。
examples.pinyin: Biǎodì sòng le wǒ yì běn hěn yǒu yìsi de shū.
examples.english: My cousin gave me a very interesting book.

components.note: 心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 总 is simplified from 總, whose threads gathered everything together.
廾 (two hands) — two hands joined — 共 is doing together; it also sounds out 供 gōng.

example.hanzi: 这次旅行总共花了三千块钱。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì lǚxíng zǒnggòng huā le sānqiān kuài qián.
example.english: This trip cost three thousand yuan altogether.
example.fact: A 2012 archaeological survey found that the Great Wall of China, counting all its branches and sections built across different dynasties, measures 21,196 kilometers altogether — more than four times earlier estimates that only counted the best-preserved Ming-era sections.

examples.hanzi: 我们班总共有三十个学生。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bān zǒnggòng yǒu sānshí gè xuésheng.
examples.english: Our class has thirty students in total.

examples.hanzi: 这些东西总共多少钱？
examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē dōngxi zǒnggòng duōshao qián?
examples.english: How much is all of this altogether?

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们; 何 was a person carrying a load (荷 hè).
可 (kě) is a close sound clue for hé; also in 河 hé, 歌 gē and 哥 gē.
夂 (foot) — stopping or going: 处 first meant to stay or settle, then a place or to deal with.

example.hanzi: 他不知道自己身在何处。
example.pinyin: Tā bù zhīdào zìjǐ shēn zài héchù.
example.english: He didn't know where he was.
example.fact: Amelia Earhart's final radio transmission on July 2, 1937, reported that she and navigator Fred Noonan did not know where they were, running low on fuel somewhere near Howland Island in the Pacific. Despite one of the largest search efforts in U.S. history at the time, the wreckage of her plane has never been conclusively found.

examples.hanzi: 你知道他现在在何处工作吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhīdào tā xiànzài zài héchù gōngzuò ma?
examples.english: Do you know where he works now?

examples.hanzi: 这个问题的答案何处可寻？
examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí de dá'àn héchù kě xún?
examples.english: Where can the answer to this question be found?

components.note: 虫 (insect) — insects and small creatures: 蚊, 蛇, 蜜; 蠢 is wriggling insects, then stupid.
春 (chūn) is a near sound match for chǔn.
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.hanzi: 年轻时谁没做过几件蠢事呢?
example.pinyin: Niánqīng shí shéi méi zuòguò jǐ jiàn chǔnshì ne?
example.english: Who hasn't done a few foolish things when they were young?
example.fact: When U.S. Secretary of State William Seward negotiated the purchase of Alaska from Russia in 1867 for $7.2 million, newspapers mocked the deal as 'Seward's Folly,' certain the frozen territory was worthless. Just thirty years later, the Klondike Gold Rush and later oil discoveries proved the acquisition to be one of the most valuable land deals in American history.

examples.hanzi: 我小时候做过很多蠢事。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎoshíhou zuò guo hěn duō chǔnshì.
examples.english: I did a lot of silly things when I was little.

examples.hanzi: 别再做这种蠢事了。
examples.pinyin: Bié zài zuò zhè zhǒng chǔnshì le.
examples.english: Don't do such a foolish thing again.

components.note: 彳 (step, conduct) — 彳 is a step or going, as in 行 and 往; 德 is conduct.
心 (heart) — 心 is the heart — the old 悳 was a straight 直 heart, so upright inner conduct.
讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话, 读; 语 is language and spoken words.
吾 (wú) — loose hint — 语 is yǔ; 吾 also sounds out 悟 wù.

example.hanzi: 她在大学里学了四年德语。
example.pinyin: Tā zài dàxué lǐ xué le sì nián Déyǔ.
example.english: She studied German for four years in university.
example.fact: German is the most widely spoken native language in the European Union, with over 95 million native speakers — more than French, Italian, or Spanish. It is also known for compound nouns of startling length, such as a 39-letter word once used in actual German legal texts to mean 'legal protection insurance companies.'

examples.hanzi: 他的德语说得很流利。
examples.pinyin: Tā de Déyǔ shuō de hěn liúlì.
examples.english: He speaks German very fluently.

examples.hanzi: 这本德语词典是朋友送我的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn Déyǔ cídiǎn shì péngyou sòng wǒ de.
examples.english: A friend gave me this German dictionary.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — a walled-in border; 固 is something fenced in and firm, as in 国 country, 围 surround.
古 (gǔ) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 故 gù, 姑 gū and 苦 kǔ.
扌 (hand) — hand radical — 执 is to hold or grasp, then carry out, as in 执行.

example.hanzi: 老人固执地拒绝去医院看病。
example.pinyin: Lǎorén gùzhí de jùjué qù yīyuàn kànbìng.
example.english: The old man stubbornly refused to go to the hospital.
example.fact: Mules are proverbially called stubborn, but animal behaviorists note their caution is really a survival trait: unlike horses, mules assess a risky situation, like an unstable bridge or unfamiliar footing, before committing, and will simply refuse to move if they judge it unsafe. That trait has kept many riders out of danger over the centuries.

examples.hanzi: 他太固执了，谁的话都不听。
examples.pinyin: Tā tài gùzhí le, shéi de huà dōu bù tīng.
examples.english: He is so stubborn that he listens to no one.

examples.hanzi: 她固执地认为自己是对的。
examples.pinyin: Tā gùzhí de rènwéi zìjǐ shì duì de.
examples.english: She stubbornly believes she is right.

components.note: 文 (writing, culture) — a person with a patterned chest, early tattooed designs, which became writing and culture. Also in 纹 wén and 蚊 wén.
子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.

example.hanzi: 她大学主修中国文学。
example.pinyin: Tā dàxué zhǔxiū Zhōngguó wénxué.
example.english: She majored in Chinese literature in college.
example.fact: Murasaki Shikibu's 'The Tale of Genji,' written in Japan around the year 1000 AD, is widely considered the world's first psychological novel. It runs to more than 1,100 pages in translation and follows over 400 characters across generations of a single imperial family.

examples.hanzi: 我最喜欢读中国古代文学。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan dú Zhōngguó gǔdài wénxué.
examples.english: I like reading ancient Chinese literature most.

examples.hanzi: 他在大学教英国文学。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài dàxué jiāo Yīngguó wénxué.
examples.english: He teaches English literature at the university.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 摄 is taking hold, then capturing on camera, as in 拍摄.
彡 (strokes of light or hair) — shining or decoration, as in 形 shape, 彩 colour, 须 beard.
景 (jǐng) is a close sound clue for yǐng; 景 itself meant light; 影 is its shadow.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌; the older meaning was a wooden mechanism.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; also in 饥 jī and 肌 jī.

example.hanzi: 剧组带来了三台摄影机拍摄这场戏。
example.pinyin: Jùzǔ dàilái le sān tái shèyǐngjī pāishè zhè chǎng xì.
example.english: The crew brought three movie cameras to film this scene.
example.fact: The Lumière brothers' Cinématographe, first demonstrated publicly in Paris in December 1895, could both film and project movies using the same hand-cranked device. Their very first films, like a fifty-second clip of workers leaving a factory, are considered among the earliest true motion pictures ever shown to a paying audience.

examples.hanzi: 摄影机一开，大家都安静下来。
examples.pinyin: Shèyǐngjī yì kāi, dàjiā dōu ānjìng xiàlái.
examples.english: Once the camera started rolling, everyone fell quiet.

examples.hanzi: 这台摄影机太重了，我拿不动。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tái shèyǐngjī tài zhòng le, wǒ ná bu dòng.
examples.english: This video camera is too heavy for me to carry.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — boundaries: 国, 园, 围; 团 is a round group. Its traditional form had 專 as sound, like 转 zhuǎn and 传 chuán.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 伙 is a companion.
火 (huǒ, fire) gives the exact sound; 火 also means fire.

example.hanzi: 警方逮捕了一个盗窃团伙。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng dàibǔ le yī gè dàoqiè tuánhuǒ.
example.english: The police arrested a theft gang.
example.fact: The Great Train Robbery of August 1963 saw a gang of fifteen men steal £2.6 million, worth well over £50 million today, from a Royal Mail train in Buckinghamshire, England. Ironically, part of the gang's downfall came from a rented farmhouse hideout where investigators later found their fingerprints on a Monopoly board they had used to pass the time.

examples.hanzi: 这个团伙专门在火车站偷东西。
examples.pinyin: Zhège tuánhuǒ zhuānmén zài huǒchēzhàn tōu dōngxi.
examples.english: This gang specialized in stealing at the train station.

examples.hanzi: 警察正在追捕这个犯罪团伙。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhèngzài zhuībǔ zhège fànzuì tuánhuǒ.
examples.english: The police are hunting down this criminal gang.

components.note: 冫 (ice, 两点水) — cold and freezing: 冰 ice, 冻 freeze, 凉 cool; here simply cold.
令 (lìng) is a loose sound clue (l- start); it also sounds out 领 lǐng and 铃 líng.
酉 (wine jar) — marks liquor and fermentation, as in 酒 liquor, 醉 drunk, 醒 sober; 酷 is strong, then harsh and cool.
告 (gào) is a loose hint for kù; 靠 kào and 浩 hào share it.

example.hanzi: 他对朋友的困境表现得很冷酷。
example.pinyin: Tā duì péngyǒu de kùnjìng biǎoxiàn de hěn lěngkù.
example.english: He was quite callous about his friend's difficulties.
example.fact: The 1964 murder of Kitty Genovese in New York City became a landmark case in social psychology after newspaper reports claimed dozens of neighbors heard her cries but did nothing to help. Although later research showed the original account was exaggerated, the case still gave rise to the term 'bystander effect,' describing how people become less likely to intervene the more witnesses are present.

examples.hanzi: 他的声音冷酷，没有一点感情。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shēngyīn lěngkù, méiyǒu yìdiǎn gǎnqíng.
examples.english: His voice was cold, without a trace of feeling.

examples.hanzi: 现实有时候很冷酷。
examples.pinyin: Xiànshí yǒushíhou hěn lěngkù.
examples.english: Reality can be harsh at times.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: voices in unison. 同 also gives sound to 铜 tóng, 桶 tǒng, 洞 dòng.

example.hanzi: 我们一同去看了那场电影。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yītóng qù kàn le nà chǎng diànyǐng.
example.english: We went to see that movie together.
example.fact: James Watson and Francis Crick worked together at Cambridge's Cavendish Laboratory to determine the double-helix structure of DNA, publishing their findings in a single one-page paper in Nature in April 1953. Their model relied heavily on X-ray diffraction images produced by their colleague Rosalind Franklin, whose contribution went largely unacknowledged at the time.

examples.hanzi: 我们一同走进了教室。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yìtóng zǒujìn le jiàoshì.
examples.english: We walked into the classroom together.

examples.hanzi: 欢迎你一同参加我们的活动。
examples.pinyin: Huānyíng nǐ yìtóng cānjiā wǒmen de huódòng.
examples.english: You're welcome to join our event with us.

components.note: 木 (wood) — beds were wooden frames; 木 is the radical of trees and wooden things like 桌 table and 椅 chair.
单 (dān) gives sound to 弹 dàn/tán and 蝉 chán; as a word it means single, alone, a list.

example.hanzi: 妈妈每周都会换洗床单。
example.pinyin: Māma měi zhōu dōu huì huànxǐ chuángdān.
example.english: Mom changes and washes the bed sheets every week.
example.fact: A typical unwashed bed sheet can host hundreds of thousands of dust mites, microscopic creatures that feed on shed human skin cells and thrive in the warm, humid environment bedding provides. Their droppings are actually a leading cause of indoor allergies, which is why sleep specialists recommend washing sheets in hot water at least once a week.

examples.hanzi: 这条床单是新买的，很软。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo chuángdān shì xīn mǎi de, hěn ruǎn.
examples.english: This bed sheet is newly bought and very soft.

examples.hanzi: 请帮我把床单铺好。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ bǎ chuángdān pūhǎo.
examples.english: Please help me spread the sheet on the bed.

components.note: 阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — hills and places: 院, 阳, 陆; 陪 is to sit by one's side.
咅 (pōu) is a loose sound clue; same part in 培 péi, 赔 péi, 倍 bèi.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter: 家, 安, 室; 审 is a hearing held in a hall.
申 (shēn) is a near sound match for shěn; also in 神 shén, 伸 shēn.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买, 货; 员 was a paid member or staff. 员 also sounds out 圆 yuán.

example.hanzi: 他被选为这次审判的陪审员。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi xuǎn wéi zhè cì shěnpàn de péishěnyuán.
example.english: He was selected as a juror for this trial.
example.fact: The tradition of a twelve-person jury traces back to medieval England, though the reason for that specific number remains uncertain — some historians link it to the twelve apostles, others to earlier Anglo-Saxon legal customs. The right to trial by a jury of one's peers was formally enshrined in the Magna Carta of 1215.

examples.hanzi: 陪审员必须听完所有的证词。
examples.pinyin: Péishěnyuán bìxū tīng wán suǒyǒu de zhèngcí.
examples.english: Jurors must listen to all of the testimony.

examples.hanzi: 十二名陪审员一致认为他有罪。
examples.pinyin: Shí'èr míng péishěnyuán yízhì rènwéi tā yǒu zuì.
examples.english: The twelve jurors unanimously agreed that he was guilty.

components.note: 疋 (foot) — the lower right. Dictionary story: an old man walking 疋 with a cane. Early forms show a person looking around, unsure. Treat as a memory aid.
矢 (arrow) — Dictionary reads it as a cane held by an old man; memory aid: an old man leaning on a stick, unsure which way — doubt, 怀疑.

example.hanzi: 我怀疑他说的不是真话。
example.pinyin: Wǒ huáiyí tā shuō de bú shì zhēnhuà.
example.english: I suspect that what he said isn't true.
example.fact: 疑 sits in 怀疑 (to doubt), 疑问 (question), 疑惑 (puzzled), 可疑 (suspicious) and 半信半疑 (half believing, half doubting). 疑 is mostly in compounds rather than alone.

examples.hanzi: 她对这个消息有点怀疑。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì zhège xiāoxi yǒudiǎn huáiyí.
examples.english: She is a bit doubtful about this news.

examples.hanzi: 这个问题没有疑问。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí méiyǒu yíwèn.
examples.english: There is no doubt about this question.

components.note: 木 (tree) — marks trees and wooden things, as in 树 tree, 林 woods, 桌 table; 桑 is the mulberry tree, whose leaves feed silkworms; 叒 above shows the many leaves.

example.hanzi: 蚕吃桑叶。
example.pinyin: Cán chī sāngyè.
example.english: Silkworms eat mulberry leaves.
example.fact: Mulberry leaves feed silkworms, which is why 桑 is tied to China's silk industry. 沧海桑田 ('blue seas turn to mulberry fields') is an idiom for great change, and 桑拿 is the loanword for sauna.

examples.hanzi: 桑树的叶子很大。
examples.pinyin: Sāngshù de yèzi hěn dà.
examples.english: The leaves of the mulberry tree are big.

examples.hanzi: 她家有一片桑园。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiā yǒu yí piàn sāngyuán.
examples.english: Her family has a mulberry orchard.

components.note: 目 (eye) — sight, as in 看, 睛, 睡.
艮 (gèn) is a loose sound clue for yǎn; 艮 also sounds out 跟 gēn, 很 hěn and 根 gēn.
目 (eye) — opening the eyes; also in 看 look, 眼 eye.
争 (zhēng) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 挣 zhèng and 筝 zhēng.
目 (eye) — opening the eyes; also in 看 look, 眼 eye.
争 (zhēng) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 挣 zhèng and 筝 zhēng.

example.hanzi: 他眼睁睁地看着机会溜走,却无能为力。
example.pinyin: Tā yǎnzhēngzhēng de kànzhe jīhuì liūzǒu, què wúnéngwéilì.
example.english: He watched helplessly as the opportunity slipped away, powerless to stop it.
example.fact: When the airship Hindenburg caught fire while landing in New Jersey in 1937, ground crew and radio announcer Herbert Morrison watched helplessly as the hydrogen-filled vessel burned and crashed in just 34 seconds. The disaster, captured on newsreel film and narrated live on radio, effectively ended the era of passenger airship travel.

examples.hanzi: 我只能眼睁睁地看着车开走了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ néng yǎnzhēngzhēng de kànzhe chē kāizǒu le.
examples.english: I could only watch helplessly as the car drove away.

examples.hanzi: 他们眼睁睁看着球掉进了水里。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen yǎnzhēngzhēng kànzhe qiú diào jìn le shuǐ lǐ.
examples.english: They watched helplessly as the ball fell into the water.

components.note: 王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 现 appear: 理 first meant polishing jade along its grain, then reason.
里 (lǐ) gives the exact sound; also in 鲤 lǐ.
木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 桌, 板: 查 first meant a raft of wood. 查 also gives 渣 zhā and 楂 zhā.
彳 (step, conduct) — 彳 is a step or going, as in 行 and 往; 德 is conduct.
心 (heart) — 心 is the heart — the old 悳 was a straight 直 heart, so upright inner conduct.

example.hanzi: 理查德是这家公司的创始人之一。
example.pinyin: Lǐchádé shì zhè jiā gōngsī de chuàngshǐrén zhī yī.
example.english: Richard is one of the founders of this company.
example.fact: In 2012, archaeologists digging beneath a parking lot in Leicester, England, discovered the skeleton of King Richard III, who had died in battle in 1485. DNA testing confirmed the identity by comparing it to living descendants of his sister, and the skeleton's curved spine matched historical accounts describing the king's scoliosis.

examples.hanzi: 理查德每天早上都去跑步。
examples.pinyin: Lǐchádé měi tiān zǎoshang dōu qù pǎobù.
examples.english: Richard goes running every morning.

examples.hanzi: 我同事理查德会说三种语言。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tóngshì Lǐchádé huì shuō sān zhǒng yǔyán.
examples.english: My colleague Richard speaks three languages.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.
比 (compare) — two people side by side, one lined up with the other; to compare.

example.hanzi: 学习一门语言好比爬一座山,需要坚持不懈。
example.pinyin: Xuéxí yī mén yǔyán hǎobǐ pá yī zuò shān, xūyào jiānchí bùxiè.
example.english: Learning a language is just like climbing a mountain — it requires persistence.
example.fact: Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay became the first climbers confirmed to reach the summit of Mount Everest in 1953, after a British expedition of over 400 people, including porters, hauled nearly 18,000 pounds of supplies to base camp. Even today, roughly one in every hundred people who attempt the summit dies in the process.

examples.hanzi: 这孩子好比一棵小树，需要慢慢长大。
examples.pinyin: Zhè háizi hǎobǐ yì kē xiǎo shù, xūyào mànmàn zhǎngdà.
examples.english: This child is like a small tree that needs time to grow.

examples.hanzi: 他对我好比亲哥哥一样。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì wǒ hǎobǐ qīn gēge yíyàng.
examples.english: He treats me just like a real older brother.

components.note: 面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.
阝 on the right is 邑 (city) — places, as in 都 capital, 邮 post, 那: a district or ministry.
咅 (pǒu) is a loose sound clue for bù; 咅 also in 剖 pōu, 培 péi and 陪 péi.

example.hanzi: 医生检查了病人的面部表情。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiǎnchá le bìngrén de miànbù biǎoqíng.
example.english: The doctor examined the patient's facial expressions.
example.fact: Psychologist Paul Ekman's research found that the human face has 43 individual muscles capable of combining into more than 10,000 distinct expressions, though only about 3,000 of these carry meaningful emotional significance. His work on universal facial expressions across cultures later inspired the animated emotions in Pixar's 'Inside Out.'

examples.hanzi: 她的面部表情看起来很紧张。
examples.pinyin: Tā de miànbù biǎoqíng kàn qǐlái hěn jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: The expression on her face looks very nervous.

examples.hanzi: 这种面霜适合用在面部。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng miànshuāng shìhé yòng zài miànbù.
examples.english: This cream is suitable for use on the face.

components.note: 自 (self) — picture of a nose; Chinese speakers point to the nose to mean "I", so it became "self" (compare 鼻 bí, nose, which adds 畀).
酋 (wine jar) with a hand 寸 offering it: honoring a guest. 尊 sounds out 遵 zūn (obey) and 樽 zūn (goblet).

example.hanzi: 每个人都应该保持自己的自尊。
example.pinyin: Měi gè rén dōu yīnggāi bǎochí zìjǐ de zìzūn.
example.english: Everyone should maintain their own self-respect.
example.fact: Psychologist Abraham Maslow placed self-esteem near the top of his 1943 hierarchy of needs, arguing that people cannot pursue their fullest potential until more basic needs for safety, belonging, and respect are met. Later research has complicated this strict ordering, showing that people facing extreme poverty or danger can still report a strong sense of purpose and self-worth.

examples.hanzi: 别人的批评伤害了他的自尊。
examples.pinyin: Biérén de pīpíng shānghài le tā de zìzūn.
examples.english: Other people's criticism hurt his pride.

examples.hanzi: 孩子也需要被尊重，要有自尊。
examples.pinyin: Háizi yě xūyào bèi zūnzhòng, yào yǒu zìzūn.
examples.english: Children also need respect and a sense of self-esteem.

components.note: 穴 (hole, cave) — 穴 marks holes and cavities, as in 空, 穷, 突; 窗 is an opening in a wall.
囱 (cōng) — near sound — 窗 is chuāng; 囱 also sounds out 葱 cōng and 聪 cōng.
口 (mouth) — a picture of an open mouth; as a radical it appears in characters of speech, eating and sounds — 吃, 喝, 叫, 吗.

example.hanzi: 阳光透过窗口照进房间。
example.pinyin: Yángguāng tòuguò chuāngkǒu zhàojìn fángjiān.
example.english: Sunlight streams through the window into the room.
example.fact: Clear flat glass windows became affordable for ordinary homes only after the float glass process was invented by Alastair Pilkington in 1959, letting molten glass flow across a bed of liquid tin to form a perfectly smooth, undistorted sheet. Before this, most window glass had faint ripples that slightly warped the view.

examples.hanzi: 请到三号窗口办理手续。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng dào sān hào chuāngkǒu bànlǐ shǒuxù.
examples.english: Please go to window number three to take care of the formalities.

examples.hanzi: 银行的窗口下午五点关门。
examples.pinyin: Yínháng de chuāngkǒu xiàwǔ wǔ diǎn guānmén.
examples.english: The bank's counter closes at five in the afternoon.

components.note: 辶 (movement) — marks roads and travel, as in 过, 进, 送; 途 is a road or route.
余 (yú) is a loose hint for tú; 涂 tú shares it.
中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.

example.hanzi: 我们在途中遇到了一场大雨。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài túzhōng yùdào le yī chǎng dàyǔ.
example.english: We ran into a heavy rain while en route.
example.fact: Ferdinand Magellan's expedition set out in 1519 with five ships and about 270 men to circumnavigate the globe, but Magellan himself was killed in the Philippines partway through the voyage. Only one ship and 18 crew members survived to complete the full journey and return to Spain three years later.

examples.hanzi: 他在去公司的途中接到了电话。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài qù gōngsī de túzhōng jiēdào le diànhuà.
examples.english: He got a phone call on his way to the company.

examples.hanzi: 旅行途中，我们拍了很多照片。
examples.pinyin: Lǚxíng túzhōng, wǒmen pāi le hěn duō zhàopiàn.
examples.english: During the trip, we took lots of photos.

components.note: 子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — money and trade: 财, 货, 买, 贵; 费 is a cost or fee.
弗 (fú) is close to fèi; same part in 沸 fèi.

example.hanzi: 这所大学的学费每年都在上涨。
example.pinyin: Zhè suǒ dàxué de xuéfèi měi nián dōu zài shàngzhǎng.
example.english: This university's tuition rises every year.
example.fact: Germany abolished tuition fees at public universities in 2014, making higher education essentially free even for international students, a policy rooted in the idea that education is a public good rather than a personal investment. By contrast, average tuition at a four-year private university in the United States that same year exceeded $30,000 per year.

examples.hanzi: 我还没交这学期的学费。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hái méi jiāo zhè xuéqī de xuéfèi.
examples.english: I haven't paid this semester's tuition yet.

examples.hanzi: 学费太贵，他只好去打工。
examples.pinyin: Xuéfèi tài guì, tā zhǐhǎo qù dǎgōng.
examples.english: The tuition was so expensive that he had to take a job.

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — 衰 once meant a rain-cape of straw, and now means decline, as in 衰老 and 衰弱.

example.hanzi: 他的身体越来越衰弱。
example.pinyin: Tā de shēntǐ yuè lái yuè shuāiruò.
example.english: His health is getting weaker and weaker.
example.fact: 衰 has the readings shuāi (decline) and cuī (mourning garments). It appears in 衰老 (age), 衰退 (recession) and 衰弱 (feeble).

examples.hanzi: 爷爷年纪大了，身体有些衰弱。
examples.pinyin: Yéye niánjì dà le, shēntǐ yǒuxiē shuāiruò.
examples.english: Grandpa is getting old and his health is a little weak.

examples.hanzi: 这个国家的经济正在衰退。
examples.pinyin: Zhège guójiā de jīngjì zhèngzài shuāituì.
examples.english: This country's economy is in decline.

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
扌 (hand) — digging by hand; also in 挖 dig, 拉 pull.
屈 (qū) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 崛 jué and 窟 kū.

example.hanzi: 考古学家在这里发掘出许多古代文物。
example.pinyin: Kǎogǔ xuéjiā zài zhèlǐ fājué chū xǔduō gǔdài wénwù.
example.english: Archaeologists excavated many ancient artifacts here.
example.fact: British archaeologist Howard Carter spent nearly five years searching the Valley of the Kings before he and his team finally excavated the largely intact tomb of Tutankhamun in November 1922. The tomb contained over 5,000 individual objects, including the pharaoh's iconic solid gold burial mask, and took nearly a decade to fully catalog and remove.

examples.hanzi: 他发掘了这个孩子的音乐天分。
examples.pinyin: Tā fājué le zhège háizi de yīnyuè tiānfèn.
examples.english: He discovered this child's musical talent.

examples.hanzi: 公司应该多发掘年轻人的潜力。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī yīnggāi duō fājué niánqīngrén de qiánlì.
examples.english: Companies should tap more into young people's potential.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
口 (mouth) — sound and speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问.
斤 (jīn, axe) is only a loose clue for tīng; the traditional 聽 had 耳 ear.

example.hanzi: 他到处打听那家餐厅的地址。
example.pinyin: Tā dàochù dǎting nà jiā cāntīng de dìzhǐ.
example.english: He asked around everywhere for that restaurant's address.
example.fact: Honeybee scouts that discover a good source of nectar perform a 'waggle dance' back at the hive, using the angle and duration of their movements to tell other bees the direction and distance to the flowers. Other bees essentially ask around by following and interpreting several dancing scouts before deciding where to fly.

examples.hanzi: 你帮我打听一下这件事好吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bāng wǒ dǎtīng yíxià zhè jiàn shì hǎo ma?
examples.english: Could you ask around about this for me?

examples.hanzi: 我想打听一下去车站怎么走。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng dǎtīng yíxià qù chēzhàn zěnme zǒu.
examples.english: I'd like to ask how to get to the station.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 拿, 抱, 把; 打 is to hit.
丁 (dīng) is a loose sound clue for dǎ; 丁 also sounds out 订 dìng, 顶 dǐng and 钉 dīng.
斗 (dipper) — a measuring dipper with a handle; as a radical it marks measuring: 料, 科, 斜. Also read dǒu (a measure) or dòu (to fight).

example.hanzi: 两只狮子为了争夺地盘而打斗。
example.pinyin: Liǎng zhī shīzi wèile zhēngduó dìpán ér dǎdòu.
example.english: The two lions fought over territory.
example.fact: Male lions that take over a new pride will often fight to the death over territory, and a successful challenger frequently kills the cubs fathered by the previous male so that the pride's lionesses come back into estrus sooner. Roughly one in four male lion cubs dies from such conflicts before reaching adulthood.

examples.hanzi: 两个醉汉在街上打斗起来。
examples.pinyin: Liǎng gè zuìhàn zài jiē shàng dǎdòu qǐlái.
examples.english: Two drunk men started fighting on the street.

examples.hanzi: 电影里有一场激烈的打斗。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ yǒu yì chǎng jīliè de dǎdòu.
examples.english: There is an intense fight scene in the movie.

components.note: 圣 (holy) — traditional 聖 had an ear 耳 and a mouth 口: the sage who listens and speaks wisely.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.
亚 (yà) — Asia; as a part it sounds out 哑 yǎ and 娅 yà.
可 (kě) doubled — a loose sound hint for gē. The same 哥 sounds out 歌 gē (song).

example.hanzi: 我们计划下个月去圣地亚哥旅游。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen jìhuà xià gè yuè qù Shèngdìyàgē lǚyóu.
example.english: We're planning a trip to Santiago next month.
example.fact: Santiago, Chile, sits within one of the most seismically active regions on Earth, part of the Pacific Ring of Fire, and the country has recorded the strongest earthquake ever measured — a magnitude 9.5 event near Valdivia in 1960. Because of this constant risk, Chilean building codes are now among the strictest in the world.

examples.hanzi: 圣地亚哥是智利的首都。
examples.pinyin: Shèngdìyàgē shì Zhìlì de shǒudū.
examples.english: Santiago is the capital of Chile.

examples.hanzi: 他在圣地亚哥住了五年。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài Shèngdìyàgē zhù le wǔ nián.
examples.english: He lived in San Diego for five years.
